Causal banking: product proposal 20 October 2026 A shared causal-analysis service Product and investment proposal 20 October 2026 Working proposal for review 1 The decision this proposal supports A universal bank needs to know when a proposed action is likely to improve a financial out- come, which assumptions make that answer possible, and when the available information cannot distinguish competing decisions. The proposed investment is a small reusable causal-analysis service supporting four journeys: funding responses, sequential servicing, intervention queries after causal discovery, and the construction of trustworthy observations. Its immediate deliverable is a bounded prototype and an evidence-based recommendation about what to build, reuse or leave unsupported. The recommendation is to develop and compare a narrow set of these operations using public records, documented public experiments and generated cases with known truth. Existing local research supplies selected working constructions and substantial negative evidence. It does not yet establish a complete product or a positive return on deployment. Expensive bank experiments should follow a prototype result that makes their cost worth considering. The absence of bank data, institutional sign-off or production access does not prevent completion of the present proposal. [1] This brief accompanies the 20 October 2026 working monograph, which has 1,162 pages and 849 audited citation records, including 213 genuine scholarly PDFs. The software, LLM/agent and integration comparisons have expanded substantially, but their coverage is still incomplete. Aggregate length does not establish completeness. Literature coverage retains the 7 October 2026 cutoff, with later acquisitions and uncertain historical versions explicitly distinguished. The recommendation remains provisional where evidence or comparison is incomplete. [40, 41] 1.1 The reusable product and its customer The first user is an analyst who can state a banking decision and inspect its assumptions. The reusable input records a target population, action and comparator, information available before the action, outcome and horizon, measurement units, observation process, causal restrictions and sampling unit. An offer, its receipt and the later balance are different variables. A measured association is not automatically the effect of changing an offer. The output keeps the target attached to its evidence. It may be an identified formula, an estimate with justified uncertainty, a set of compatible effects, an informative refusal or a failed computation. Unresolved graph endpoints, unbounded confidence sets and numerical failures require different responses. The library, command line and MCP interface should preserve these distinctions so that a downstream application can decide whether to act, ask for information or fall back to its existing workflow. A callable endpoint alone does not establish identification, useful precision or interoperability. [42] The shared layer would organize three workspaces: intervention studies, sequential decisions and dynamic systems. The four banking journeys pass through these workspaces, with observation quality affecting all three. This organization avoids building a separate estimation stack for every business team while retaining each team’s population, timing and economic account. The initial service would require analyst review of consequential scientific choices. No autonomous bank action is proposed. 1.2 A concrete first slice A useful first demonstration begins with a public or generated business brief, constructs an explicit question and alternative diagrams, checks the available identification route, and returns a result whose assumptions and information limits remain visible through the library, CLI and MCP. For a randomized offer, the first target can be the effect of assignment. A receipt effect requires additional compliance and exclusion assumptions. For a confounded observational table, the correct result may be a documented ambiguity rather than a number. The comparison must include an expert-designed template and a directly composed existing- package workflow. The new service earns its place only if the common representation and checks reduce consequential mistakes or repeated effort without discarding valid alternatives. A generated example can expose a wrong answer cheaply; it cannot establish how often the same failure occurs at a bank. 2 Causal banking: product proposal 20 October 2026 2 What the evidence currently supports 2.1 Funding and observations Earlier registered synthetic funding work found a passing construction under a demanding information design: known randomized action moments, truthful sampled links, known inclusion probabilities and independent calendars. Its six valid cells passed the prespecified minimum- coverage screen. False exogeneity, wrong inclusion probabilities and label errors retained adverse findings. This supports a selected procedure conditional on its information law, rather than a general correction for one dependent bank panel. [43] The newer joint-dependence argument makes that limitation more explicit. A finite confidence- region construction can use declared nuisance bounds and conservative projection. Its representative precision is inadequate under the reviewed design. An exact persistence argument also shows why an unrestricted claim cannot obtain useful shrinking uncertainty merely by lengthening a single highly persistent series. The practical next choices are to narrow the dependence family, obtain justified additional information, or accept wider and possibly unbounded results. The new derivation has not been turned into a qualified numerical projection service. [44] Observation linkage is part of the scientific problem. If different customer histories are obser- vationally compatible but imply different intervention values, more computation on the same summaries cannot choose among them. Public/generated linkage cases can test whether the prototype preserves this ambiguity. A later bank study would need representative truth labels and an explicit inclusion mechanism; labels with unknown selection do not establish the same result. [45, 44] 2.2 Servicing and learned policies Selected earlier servicing studies support fixed-policy inference in a restricted nonlinear family under truthful state audits, supplied historical action probabilities and independent customer trajectories. Their wrong-logger and information-leakage cases remain failures. They do not establish the value of an unrestricted learned policy with hidden borrower state. [46] A new argument handles estimated action and observation probabilities in a finite, prespecified history table with bounded rewards. It separates training from evaluation and makes the support and observation assumptions explicit. Exact calculations check its policy-value identities and counterexamples. Its conservative uncertainty can nevertheless exceed the complete target range at a representative sample size. The public servicing design uses continuous histories and unbounded Gaussian/quadratic quantities, so this finite-table theorem cannot simply be attached to that design. A useful next study needs a reviewed tighter argument, a separately declared bounded target, or a different experiment. It must preserve the failed predecessor rather than change the target after evaluation. [47] 2.3 Discovery and agent support Graph discovery constrains possible relationships under stated assumptions. It may return an equivalence class whose members imply different interventions. The proposed service must retain that class and distinguish uncertainty in graph learning from uncertainty in an effect. Exact latent-risk examples in the current comparison exhibit identical observed Gaussian distributions with action effects of zero and three fifths. They prove nonidentification within a class containing both models; they do not enumerate the entire identified set. [48] LLMs are proposed as aids for translating business language, finding missing timing definitions, 3 Causal banking: product proposal 20 October 2026 suggesting diagrams and alternatives, and preparing auditable tool requests. A model-generated diagram is a candidate assumption, not observed causal truth. The evaluation must score false confidence, unsupported orientations, omitted alternatives and appropriate requests for information. Deterministic task fixtures and exact examples already support some checks; no live- model superiority or bank decision gain is established by the new task designs. A live comparison would require a frozen backend, held-out tasks, reference adjudication, costs and equally informed baselines. [42] 3.1 What the expanded interface work now demonstrates The proposal now develops request admission, result interpretation, publication integrity, retention and capacity as parts of the same workflow. A local standalone-client check made six actual library and CLI calls across three requests: a conditional expression, an unsupported sampling setting and a contradicted premise. Their scientific meanings agreed. Four effect-set examples were preserved response replays; they were not four fresh calculations. Five malformed replies were rejected. This evidence supports the inspected local examples and their declared schemas. It does not establish a running notebook kernel, a newly executed MCP integration, another repository’s adoption or production service levels. [58] The retention argument is likewise a design result with a finite reference. Across ten allowed publication/collection orders, a stale-snapshot collector loses an artifact needed by a live request in three orders. A coordinated recheck against current roots avoids that failure in all ten, with nine successful publications and one safe rejection. This motivates pins, a live-root check and an explicit rule for stale publishers. It is not an estimated failure probability or an implemented storage collector. The prototype should test those semantics under realistic interruption and restart before an operating guarantee is proposed. [59] 3.2 What Bayesian advice adds, and what it cannot justify A corrected University of Sao Paulo thesis, published before the cutoff, supplies a useful adverse comparison for LLM-assisted graph discovery. Its reported DiBS graph-distance results improve with a GPT prior on Sachs but worsen on MAGIC-7, MAGIC-ORIGINAL and the authored Summer case. A DeepSeek prior improves the Summer result while worsening the two smaller reported alternatives. These are the thesis’s tabulated means, not new experimental runs or signif- icance tests. The integrated discussion retains its selected feedback experiments, omitted adverse trials and appendix reproducibility discrepancies. It therefore supports an experiment comparing information channels, rather than a claim that LLM advice improves discovery universally. [60] Repeated model answers estimate response behavior under the query mechanism. A model can 5 Causal banking: product proposal 20 October 2026 repeat a correct or an incorrect answer equally consistently. The exact examples in the monograph also show that restricting an edge model to legal graphs changes its marginal probabilities, and that a Bayesian feedback update is justified only by its stipulated likelihood. A proposed deposit-diagram assistant should preserve response frequencies, semantic categories, admitted graph support and the evidence for adviser accuracy separately. Adopt these design lessons now; defer executable DiBS, ancestral-graph or DSPy integration until pinned code, rights, prompts and experiment artifacts have been inspected. [61, 60] 3.3 R identification and framework evaluation The expanded R comparison distinguishes graphical adjustment, symbolic ID/IDC, counterfactual identification, restricted sharp bounds and Bayesian causal queries. These operations answer different questions. In an exact authored repayment example, a point-identified average effect coexists with a nontrivial counterfactual interval, while two admissible priors give different posterior summaries. The supplied assumptions and result type therefore need to survive any language adapter. Selected pinned sources support the comparison; native R execution, broader census and complete dependency/rights qualification remain unresolved. The causaleffect disposition is reference use with executable integration deferred. [62] Two additional originals help specify a framework comparison. The selected autonomous-agent survey organizes profile, memory, planning and action, and discusses prompt fragility, hallucination, information leakage and efficiency. PromptBench provides a documented modular evaluation design and custom metric hooks; its historical findings do not show that one prompt is best for every task. These sources support a proposed evaluator whose references check the banking target, assumptions and valid nonidentification responses. They do not establish a qualified causal agent, current model ranking or licensed software integration. [63, 64] An exact bookkeeping illustration separates completion from correctness. Across forty fixed requests in twenty paired families, stipulated system A has 22 correct, two wrong and sixteen unanswered requests; B has thirty correct, six wrong and four unanswered. Accuracy among completed requests favors A, whereas correct responses per planned request favor B. With assumed value and error costs, their net-value ranking can reverse. These are authored outcomes and prices, not observed model or bank performance. A justified scientific refusal can be a completed correct answer; an execution failure remains in the planned denominator. The comparison should preserve both distinctions and pairing. [82, 83, 84, 76] 7 Causal banking: product proposal 3.6 20 October 2026 Causal-agent ambition, evidence and the decision being answered Two selected originals sharpen what the proposed agent should do. The biomedical position paper proposes linking language models, structured knowledge, heterogeneous observations and formal causal tools. It supplies an agenda for controlled actions, verification and evaluation, not a new qualified end-to-end causal agent. A philosophical neuron-diagram study supplies a mechanism and asks whether events occur and what causes them. Its small historical examples and proposed DEF-1 attribution rule do not measure statistical discovery from unrestricted data or general current model competence. The study’s selected diagrams also helped develop its labeling rule. The monograph records a citation-chain mismatch in the biomedical discussion and localized explanatory and target inconsistencies in the diagram transcripts. Each requires resolution before the affected source path or case becomes an admitted benchmark. [85, 86] A new exact servicing example separates causal attribution from incremental value. The stipulated priority route suppresses an available backup; either executed route succeeds. Removing priority alone restores the backup, whereas removing both priority and backup removes recovery. With assumed USD 200 success value, USD 40 priority cost and USD 10 executed-backup cost, priority returns USD 160 net and backup USD 190 when backup is available. Priority thus provides the factual recovery path while adding minus USD 30 net value. If backup availability is unknown before action and has stipulated probability p, priority’s expected advantage is 160 − 190p USD per case, positive exactly when p < 16/19. This is an authored structural and monetary construction, not a DEF-1 implementation, model trial or bank ROI. [87] The prototype recommendation is to evaluate mechanism propagation, attribution, intervention semantics and prospective value as distinct tasks. Freeze the rubric before evaluation, adjudicate disputed transcripts, and keep generated graph families separate from those used to develop the rules. Public and synthetic evidence can establish whether the proposed interfaces preserve those contracts and whether further experiments are worthwhile. [102] An authored ten-request example uses 23 attempts for six eventual test successes, of which four satisfy a separate causal acceptance check. With assumed USD 2 per attempt and USD 15 per accepted output, cost is USD 46, cost per acceptance USD 11.50 and net value USD 14. Treating all six test passes as accepted produces USD 44 net and overstates value by USD 30. Actual prices and bank ROI remain unknown. Freeze the corpus/exclusions, model and environment, hold final causal acceptance tests outside adaptive feedback, include misleading and missing evidence, and retain every failed attempt and cost. Require correct estimands, clocks, graph/identification scope, uncertainty and justified refusal before counting an output as accepted. Resolve the study’s real artifact and inspect any adopted package originals before executable admission. [101, 102, 103] 3.14 EconML: a reference choice with target and history safeguards The selected EconML source, at a 1 October 2026 commit declaring version 0.17.0, is a useful reference for heterogeneous effects and selected dynamic-panel comparisons. Its effect model and supplied prediction population determine what is averaged. A flexible nuisance learner cannot correct an omitted effect modifier by itself. The proposed adapter must preserve the action contrast, pre-action adjustment, effect-function class, population and monetary units. This is a completed proposal choice; executable integration remains deferred. [104] An exact authored example assigns half the customers to each of two observed strata. Offer probabilities are one half and one tenth, while stratum effects are USD 0 and USD 100. The population effect is USD 50. A deliberately misspecified constant residual regression instead targets USD 450/17, about USD 26.47, because it weights strata by treatment variation. At an assumed cost of USD 35, the population decision has net value USD 15; mislabelling the projection gives about USD -8.53. This is target misspecification, not a reported library error under a correct effect model. [105] The selected dynamic path infers periods from row occurrence inside a customer, requires equal history lengths and ignores supplied sample weights and sample variances with a warning. The inspected bootstrap call path resamples time rows inside fixed customer groups, so it can duplicate or reverse a history. An authored two-date enumeration preserves the original ordered history in only one of four equally likely row draws. No installed EconML bootstrap was run, and this is not a measured coverage failure. Group-aware nuisance folds and within-unit covariance also do not establish protection against common calendar shocks across customers. [104, 105] Start with a narrow public or synthetic static prototype, using exact nuisance and target references. Then test chronological unit/time conversion, weight refusal, actual bootstrap draws, warnings and declared sampling laws before admitting a dynamic adapter. Preserve applicable MIT and BSD notices, lock package and native dependencies, and measure fitting, resampling, failed-run and maintenance costs. A Python boundary is a candidate; a wholesale port is not justified by the present evidence. Public conformance can establish whether this route merits later bank trials. Lin’s methodological workflow separates research tools, model evaluation, human simulation and cognitive explanation, and calls for instrument validation, held-out assessment, controlled execution and analysis that respects dependence. It offers a design framework and illustrative code, not an empirical validation of a banking assistant. [143] An exact proposal example makes the investment implication visible. True correctness is 60% in both workflows. The first grader sensitivity and specificity are 80% and 90%; for the second workflow they are 95% and 80%. Observed passing rises from 52% to 65% despite unchanged correctness. Under an assumed value of USD 100 per additional correct result and extra workflow cost of USD 8, the grade-based incremental value is USD 5 while the true incremental value is USD -8. These are imposed probabilities and planning values. Held-out calibration and its uncertainty are necessary before correcting real scores. Repeated answers do not create independent scenarios; averaging cannot remove shared environmental shocks. Costs should include grading and adjudication as well as model execution. This defines a prototype evaluation to justify later bank experiments; it does not claim that such an experiment has been run. 3.24 Use expert-guided ensembles to propose graphs with explicit limits Tench and Demeester combine discovery algorithms by counting connections, separating orientation, checking cycles and querying an expert on selected disagreements. [166] 5 Economics and the next experiment Let N be the number of attempted decision tasks in one year, D the incremental gross monetary utility of the proposed action relative to the chosen baseline, F fixed incremental cost, c variable incremental cost per attempted task, and R an additional risk cost not already counted in D. A transparent planning account is V = N E[D] − F − N c − R. The baseline must be a feasible alternative under the same information. A correct refusal may leave the baseline action unchanged while still costing review time. A misleading recommendation can have negative utility. Loss must not be counted in both D and R, and unacceptable actions remain excluded by constraints irrespective of their average financial payoff. [166] 5.1 A reproducible illustration, with assumed inputs The following one-year illustration uses USD solely as a declared planning unit. Assume 10,000 attempted tasks, fixed incremental cost of USD 100,000, variable incremental cost of USD 6 per task and no separate R. All volumes, prices, gains, probabilities and signal likelihoods below are assumptions; none is a measured bank benefit or vendor quote. The calculation excludes discounting because its horizon is one year. [166] 21 Causal banking: product proposal 20 October 2026 Regime Prior Gross gain/task Net value Pr(positive signal) High Moderate Adverse 0.4 0.4 0.2 USD 40 USD 20 USD −2 USD 240,000 USD 40,000 USD −180, 000 0.8 0.5 0.1 Expected incremental value is USD 76,000 before further information. This number alone cannot justify a real investment because its inputs are assumed. Under the same assumptions, an experiment produces a positive signal with probability 0.54. Expected net value conditional on that signal is approximately USD 150,370, and conditional on a negative signal it is approximately minus USD 11,304. Choosing to build only after a positive signal gives expected value USD 81,200 before the experiment’s own cost. The expected value of sample information is consequently USD 5,200. An experiment costing USD 8,000 loses USD 2,800 in expected information value; at USD 3,000 it gains USD 2,200, assuming identical signal informativeness. Perfect information has value USD 36,000 in this illustration. That is an upper bound on the information component of spending for this particular decision and prior, not a universal experiment budget. The prototype must help assess the assumed signal quality before these calculations can inform an expensive study. [166] Holding other assumptions fixed, break-even gross gain is USD 16 per attempted task. Halving volume raises it to USD 26; doubling volume reduces it to USD 11. An additional USD 4 of review cost per task raises the 10,000-task threshold to USD 20. These sensitivities are arithmetic consequences, not estimates of demand or analyst effort. Refusals and failed requests still incur applicable costs and remain among the attempted tasks. [167] 5.2 Costs to measure in the prototype The measured account should separate data acquisition and cleaning, labels and identity audits, model and tool calls, analyst formulation and checking, package setup, integration and maintenance, compute and storage, incident recovery and independent validation. Each cost needs its unit, quantity, date/version, price source and incremental share relative to the baseline. The current actual-price fields remain unfilled. Public examples can reveal setup burden and local resource use without establishing bank-scale service levels, customer outcomes or willingness to adopt. [166] A later bank experiment should state the decisions it distinguishes, the uncertain assumption that matters, the target population and horizon, expected signals, losses from wrong decisions, and the full cost of obtaining the information. It should compare cheaper public/generated alternatives first. If no feasible experiment has plausible positive net information value, narrow or defer the capability. A demand for authentic evidence becomes appropriate when that specific experiment is justified; it is not a prerequisite for writing the current proposal. 6 What remains before a complete proposal The software comparison still has 68 open and 32 inconclusive cells in its 102-cell coverage matrix. The reuse register has 89 open and three inconclusive decisions among 115 candidates. These counts describe unresolved review obligations, not numbers of defective products. Each closure needs an explicit original, supported scope, comparison and adopt/integrate/port/reject decision. No absence finding follows from an unread source. [168, 169, 170, 171, 172, 173, 174, 175, 176, 177, 178] Twenty of 22 chapter reviews meet their current author criteria. L1 and L6 remain inconclusive because frontier and framework coverage is incomplete despite meeting minimum depth. The 22 Causal banking: product proposal 20 October 2026 original-candidate census now contains 54 inspected and 59 unread originals out of 113; citation- chain leads retain their own denominator. Fourteen task reviews and all twelve integration requirements have scoped proposal outcomes, but those receipts do not establish a live model benchmark or cross-repository adoption. The three mandatory repairs remain open. The agreed depth contracts retain 100–150 substantive software pages, approximately 100 agent pages and a developed integration treatment; repeated material does not earn duplicate credit. [168, 179, 180, 181, 1] The current sponsor update reconciles the recommendation, selected new evidence and remaining work to this reader. Final proposal acceptance still requires complete coverage reconciliation and rendered visual review of the exact release. Source audits, exact arithmetic and all-page text bounds are narrower checks and cannot substitute for visual acceptance. Missing bank data, platform access or signed adoption remain later conditional needs; they do not stop independent proposal research. [2, 168] The evidence routes are also different. We know how to complete missing source comparisons, write and test selected adapters, run registered generated benchmarks and measure local workflow costs. Their success still requires execution and review. We do not presently have a general useful solution for arbitrary latent graphs, unrestricted persistent dependence, hidden-state optimal policies or arbitrary nuisance learners. The proposal can be complete with explicit bounded claims and negative findings in these areas; it cannot claim their scientific resolution. [2, 44, 47] The present recommendation is therefore to test the narrow common service against existing composition, use that evidence to refine the investment scenario, and request a bank experiment only for a consequential question that the cheaper evidence cannot settle. Independent scientific acceptance, target-bank validation, production reliability and adoption are later decisions with their own evidence. They remain distinct from completing a credible proposal and a useful bounded prototype. 23 Causal banking: product proposal 20 October 2026 References [1] Causal banking proposal project.
